verdict.rationale: Community evidence indicates Mastra's source is published under the Elastic License v2. That makes the code readable, but ELv2 bars offering it as a hosted or managed service, so it only partly meets the 'open license' bar, and a commenter explicitly argues it isn't open source. No first-party license page or repository link appears in the pack. Missing for 10: first-party documentation of the license and source repository, an OSI-approved open license without use restrictions, independent confirmation of source availability.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can read the product's source under an open license

citations.quote: Mastra uses the Elastic v2 license, which says 'You may not provide the software to third parties as a hosted or managed service'
